question.problem:
Find a parametric equation of the osculating plane for the curve  $r(t)$ at the point where $t=\pi $, given that

$$
r(t)=⟨t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,T(\pi )=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,0,-1⟩,\,N(\pi )=⟨0,1,0⟩.
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
The osculating plane passes through the point $P$, which is at the tip of the vector $r(\pi ).$ The vectors $T(\pi )$ and $N(\pi )$ are parallel to this plane. Therefore, a parametric equation for the plane can be written as

$$
R(s,u)=r(\pi )+s\,T(\pi )+u\,N(\pi ),\,s,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

 

We have that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\pi ) & =⟨\pi ,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩=⟨\pi ,-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, a parametric equation for the osculating plane at the point $(\pi ,-1,0)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s,u) & =r(\pi )+s\,T(\pi )+u\,N(\pi ) \\  & =⟨\pi ,-1,0⟩+s\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨1,0,-1⟩+u\cdot ⟨0,1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨2\pi +\sqrt{2}s,\,-2+2u,\,-\sqrt{2}s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
